Firefox's Bookmarks toolbar gives you quick access to often-used bookmarks. This article describes how to use the Bookmarks toolbar and how to hide it.
;[[Image:Fx155Toolbar-Bookmarks]]
For more information on bookmarks, see the [[Bookmarks in Firefox]] article.

__TOC__

=Show or hide the Bookmarks toolbar=
The Bookmarks toolbar is shown by default on the [[New Tab page in Firefox|New Tab page]] but you can also show it on all pages, or it can be hidden.

To show or hide the Bookmarks toolbar:
{for win, linux}
#[[T:customizefx29]]
#Click the {menu Toolbars} button at the bottom of the screen.
#;{for win}[[Image:Fx85BetaCustomizeToolbars-win]]{/for}
#Go to the {menu Bookmarks Toolbar} menu and choose one of these settings:
#*{menu Always Show} will show the Bookmarks toolbar on all pages.
#*{menu Never Show} will hide it on all pages.
#*{menu Only Show on New Tab} will show the Bookmarks toolbar only on the New Tab page.
#Click {button Done}.
{note}'''Tip:''' Another way to show or hide the Bookmarks Toolbar is to right-click a blank spot on the Tab bar at the top of the Firefox window, find {menu Bookmarks Toolbar} in the context menu and choose your preferred setting.{/note}
{/for}
{for mac}
#Click {menu View} in the Firefox menu bar at the top of the screen.
#Go down to the {menu Toolbars} menu and select {menu Bookmarks Toolbar}.
#;[[Image:Fx155Mac-View-Toolbars-Bookmarks]]
#Choose one of these settings:
#*{menu Always Show} will show the Bookmarks toolbar on all pages.
#*{menu Never Show} will hide it on all pages.
#*{menu Only Show on New Tab} will show the Bookmarks toolbar only on the New Tab page.
{note}'''Note:''' You can also use the [[Customize Firefox controls, buttons and toolbars|Customize]] menu to show or hide the Bookmarks toolbar.{/note}
{/for}

==Remove or restore Other Bookmarks folder==
If the Other Booksmarks folder in your Bookmarks Library contains any bookmarks, an '''Other Bookmarks folder''' icon will appear at the end of the Bookmarks toolbar by default.
To remove it from the Bookmarks toolbar:
#[[Template:contextmenu]] on a blank spot at the end of the Bookmarks toolbar (or on the ''Other Bookmarks'' folder icon) to open the context menu.
#;[[Image:Fx91BookmarksToolbarContextMenu]]
#Click on the {menu Show Other Bookmarks} menu item to remove the check mark.
To later restore the Bookmarks toolbar ''Other Bookmarks'' folder icon, {for win,linux}right-click{/for}{for mac}hold down the {key control} key while you click{/for} on a blank spot at the end of the Bookmarks toolbar and then click on the {menu Show Other Bookmarks} menu item to add back the check mark.

=Add bookmarks to the Bookmarks toolbar=
#Set the Bookmarks toolbar to {menu Always Show} ([[#w_show-or-hide-the-bookmarks-toolbar|see above]]) so that you can see it on all pages.
#Go to the page you want to add to the Bookmarks toolbar.
#In the address bar, click and drag the padlock icon onto the Bookmarks toolbar.
#;[[Image:AddBookmarkToolbar]]
After adding bookmarks, you can reset the Bookmarks toolbar to your preferred setting.

=Re-order bookmarks on the Bookmarks toolbar=
To change the position of an item on the Bookmarks toolbar, click and hold the bookmark or folder you want to move and then drag it into position.

=Add toolbar items to the Bookmarks toolbar=
The Bookmarks toolbar can have items other than bookmarks added to it. For more information, see [[Customize Firefox controls, buttons and toolbars]].

=Bookmarks toolbar not showing=
If the bookmarks toolbar is still not visible after following the steps in the [[#w_show-or-hide-the-bookmarks-toolbar|Show or hide the Bookmarks toolbar]] section, try the following solutions.

==Check if Firefox is in Full Screen mode==
The toolbar is hidden by default in Full Screen mode. To check if Firefox is in Full Screen mode:
#{for win, linux}Press {key F11}{/for}{for mac}Press the keyboard shortcut {key Control+Command+F}{/for} to exit Full Screen mode.
#Move the cursor to the top of the screen. If the toolbar appears, Full Screen mode was likely the cause.

==Check if the Bookmarks Toolbar is set to {menu Only show on new tab}==
Sometimes the toolbar is set to appear only on new tabs. To check this setting:
#Right-click an empty area of the toolbar or tab bar.
#Hover over the {menu Bookmarks Toolbar} menu and select {menu Always Show} from the displayed options.

==Restore default toolbar settings==
A custom configuration may be hiding the toolbar. To restore the default toolbar settings:
#Right-click an empty area of the toolbar or tab bar.
#Select {menu Customize Toolbar…}.
#Click the {button Restore Defaults} button in the bottom-right corner of the window.
#Click the {button Done} button.

==Restart Firefox or check for updates==
An outdated or corrupted session may prevent changes from taking effect.

===Restart Firefox===
Close and reopen Firefox.

===Update Firefox===
To check for updates:
#{for win, linux}Press the {key Alt} key. In the menu bar that appears, click {menu Help}{/for}{for mac}In the menu bar, click {menu Firefox}{/for} and select {menu About Firefox}. The ''About Firefox'' window will open. If an update is available, it will be installed.
#Click the {button Restart to update Firefox} button after the update is installed.
#If Firefox is up to date, close the window.

==Check extensions or themes that may interfere==
Some extensions or themes may affect toolbar visibility. To check installed extensions:
#Click the Firefox menu [[Image:firefoxmenu]] and select {menu Add-ons and themes}. The Add-ons Manager (''about:addons'') will open with the ''Extensions'' panel active.
#Disable extensions one by one to check if any of them is causing the issue.

To check installed themes:
#Click {menu Themes} in the left panel of the Add-ons Manager.
#If a custom theme is in use, switch back to the system theme.
